title: Rapid model reversion negotiation and KV cache reconciliation for multi-tenant canary regressions
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Investigate and execute a coordinated rollback and KV cache reconciliation after multiple tenants reported semantic regressions during a model canary on hosted and dedicated planes. Ensure minimally disruptive mitigation, tenant-prioritized hotpatching where needed, and clear customer communication.
runbook_steps: 1) Triage: confirm regression signature (latency vs semantic) and map affected tenant slices via telemetry and request traces
2) Stabilize traffic: flip canary -> 0% for impacted slices; apply circuit-breaker at gateway level for mixed-topology tenants
3) Pin model: for affected tenants in Dedicated/Private, pin to last-known-good model version at router level
4) KV cache reconciliation: initiate staged KV drain with per-slice rehydration to prevent stale-cache artifacts (see KV reconciliation playbook)
5) Hotpatch: if code-level fix needed, prepare livepatch branch and coordinate canary rollback to staging, then apply to canary subset
6) Communication: send tenant-facing status update with expected timeline and mitigation steps
7) Post-stabilization: run regression evals on pinned and candidate models; schedule full rollout only after quality gates pass
8) Postmortem: capture root cause, metrics delta, and recommended runtime changes (automatic slice quarantine, faster rollback hooks)
immediate_actions: 03/10 09:12 UTC - Pager triggered by semantic-degradation alert for canary-variant v2026-03-alpha
03/10 09:20 UTC - Scoped affected tenants via trace ids; 7 tenants show >10% semantic errors vs baseline
03/10 09:25 UTC - Routed canary traffic to fallback v2026-02-stable for hosted tier; began tenant pin for 3 Dedicated customers
03/10 09:40 UTC - Opened customer bridge with SRE, Solutions Eng, and PM; initial customer comms drafted (see communications_template link)
03/11 02:10 UTC - Identified KV cache eviction race in runtime kernel on sequence length >1024 causing stale prefix exposures; reproduction PR created
forensics_summary: Root cause: kernel-level KV eviction race in async batch path exposed stale prefixes when rolling between model variants under mixed batching
Manifestation: semantic hallucinations for prompts with long context lengths, amplified on Dedicated pools with heterogeneous batchers
Scope: ~0.6% of requests in canary slice, but affected tenants reported high-impact user-visible failures
Mitigation path: model pinning + KV drain + livepatch to fix eviction scheduling; longer-term: add eviction backpressure and deterministic KV drains on variant switch
customer_communication_template: We are aware of regressions affecting a subset of customers during a recent model canary rollout. Our engineers have isolated the issue to a cache eviction race and have rolled the affected tenants back to the previous model. We will continue to monitor and will follow up with a timeline for a safe re-rollout and postmortem within 72 hours.

Can Solutions Eng apply tenant-level rehydration for on-prem customers without downtime?
Is there a short-term telemetry flag we can add to detect eviction races proactively?
